noteRef.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specPoints.text: understand the concepts of homologous series and functional group

primer.text: Organic chemistry runs on families: a homologous series shares one functional group and climbs by CH2 steps, its chemistry constant while boiling points and densities drift upward. The functional group is the property engine, and R - any group except hydrogen - generalises it across skeletons. This note defines the series and reads the groups table.

lessons.title: Families that grow by CH2
lessons.opening: A homologous series is organic chemistry's family tree: compounds sharing one functional group, each successive member one CH2 longer than the last. Members share a general formula and near-identical chemistry, while their physical properties - boiling point, melting point, density - slide gradually as the molecules grow. Ethanol to propanol is exactly one CH2 step; the alkane series is the classic ladder.
keyPoints: Members of a homologous series all carry the same functional group.
Each successive member differs by a CH2 unit.
Every member shares the same general formula and similar chemical properties.
Physical properties - boiling point, melting point, density - change gradually along the series.
Ascending the series enlarges the molecules, shifting those physical properties.

low.restatement: Same reactive group, same formula pattern, one CH2 per rung: the family climbs a ladder of ever-so-slightly heavier molecules.
low.analogy: One house design (functional group) built on plots of growing size: same layout, steadily larger garden each step.
low.examPointer: The CH2 increment is the definitional phrase - quote 'successive members differ by CH2' verbatim.

medium.restatement: The series is defined chemically (shared functional group and general formula) and graded physically: each CH2 addition raises molecular size, so dispersion-driven properties like boiling point and density climb gradually while reactivity stays put.
medium.analogy: A staircase where every step is the same height (CH2) but the view (physical properties) changes slowly with altitude.
medium.examPointer: Distinguish the invariants (functional group, general formula, chemical properties) from the sliders (boiling point, melting point, density).

check.stem: What must every member of a homologous series share?

options.explanation: That is the defining membership test.

options.text: The same number of carbon atoms
options.explanation: Members differ by CH2, so carbon counts grow.
Physical properties change gradually, not identically.

check.stem: By how much does each successive member of a homologous series differ?

options.explanation: The definitional increment of the family.
No CH3 increment exists in the definition.
The step adds carbon AND two hydrogens together.

check.stem: What happens to physical properties as a homologous series is ascended?

options.text: They change gradually as the molecules increase in size
options.explanation: Boiling point, melting point and density slide along the ladder.

options.text: They change randomly from member to member
options.explanation: The change is gradual and systematic.

options.text: They all jump sharply at each step
options.explanation: The changes are gradual, not jumps.

check.stem: Why do ethanol and propanol sit in one homologous series?

options.text: they share the same functional group and propanol is one CH2 longer
options.explanation: One increment up the same family ladder.

options.text: they have the same number of hydrogens
one is the alkane series member

check.stem: Which set of properties would you expect to be SIMILAR across a homologous series?

options.text: Chemical properties, because the functional group is shared

check.modelAnswer: A homologous series gathers organic compounds sharing one functional group, and each step up the series adds a CH2.

check.stem: State what members of a homologous series share and what changes gradually.
check.modelAnswer: They share the functional group, general formula and similar chemical properties; boiling point, melting point and density change gradually.

check.stem: Explain why ascending a homologous series changes boiling point but not chemical behaviour.
check.modelAnswer: Each CH2 step enlarges the molecule, raising the intermolecular attractions that boiling must overcome, while the reactive site - the functional group - stays identical, so the chemistry is unchanged.

check.stem: An unknown alcohol sits two rungs above ethanol in its series. State the increment between them and the effect on boiling point.
check.modelAnswer: Two successive CH2 increments separate them - two CH2 units in total - so the unknown is larger and boils higher than ethanol, with the change gradual across the two steps.

lessons.title: Functional groups run the show
sourceHeadings: Functional Groups Found in Compounds Table
lessons.opening: The functional group is the business end of an organic molecule: the atom or group that determines its physical and chemical properties. In the common-groups table, R is the placeholder for whatever other atom or atom-cluster the molecule carries, hydrogen excepted - one group pattern, a whole family of compounds.
keyPoints: Physical behaviour and chemical reactivity both flow from the functional group.
The common functional groups are summarised in a reference table.
R is the stand-in for any other atom or atom-group - hydrogen excluded.
Identifying the functional group identifies the reactive behaviour of the compound.
The same group pattern in different molecules places them in the same homologous series.

low.restatement: Find the functional group and you have found the molecule's personality: how it reacts and much of how it behaves.
low.analogy: The engine in a car: body and colour vary (the R group), but the engine decides how it drives.
low.examPointer: Remember R's restriction: any atom or group EXCEPT hydrogen - hydrogen gets its own explicit slot in the tables.

medium.restatement: Functional groups are the reactive determinants of organic chemistry: the group's bonding pattern fixes both the chemical reactions available and the physical behaviour of the class, while R generalises the pattern across every carbon skeleton except bare hydrogen.
medium.analogy: A USB port standardises what any device can do regardless of its housing - the group defines the interface, R is the housing.
medium.examPointer: When asked to identify a series or predict reactions, point at the functional group first and the R group second.

check.stem: In functional-group tables, what does R represent?

options.text: Whatever other atom or atom-cluster the molecule carries, hydrogen barred

options.explanation: R is a placeholder, not an operator.

check.stem: Why do ethanol and propanol share their chemical reactivity?

options.text: Both carry the same functional group, which runs their chemistry
options.explanation: The shared group gives shared reactions.

options.text: They have the same boiling point

options.explanation: They belong to the alcohol series.

check.stem: A molecule's formula changes but its functional group stays the same. What happens to its chemistry?

options.text: Its chemical properties stay essentially the same, run by the unchanged group

options.explanation: The group, not the chain, drives reactivity.

options.text: It becomes a different homologous series
options.explanation: The same group keeps it in the same series.

check.stem: Where would you look up the pattern of a functional group you need to identify?

options.text: In the summary table of common functional groups found in compounds
options.explanation: The table is the reference of record.
The periodic table lists elements, not organic groups.

options.text: Nowhere - they must be memorised without patterns

check.stem: State the role of a functional group in a molecule.
check.modelAnswer: The functional group determines the physical and chemical properties of the molecule.

check.stem: State what R stands for in the functional-group table.
check.modelAnswer: R stands for whatever other atom or atom-cluster the molecule carries, with hydrogen explicitly excluded.

check.stem: Explain why the functional group, rather than the carbon chain, decides a molecule's reactions.
check.modelAnswer: Reactions happen at sites of particular bonding patterns, and the functional group is exactly that site; the carbon chain is mostly spectator framework, so swapping CH2 units leaves the reactive behaviour in place.

check.stem: Two molecules share a functional group but differ by three CH2 units. Predict their relative reactivity and boiling points.
check.modelAnswer: Their reactivity is similar - the same group runs both - while the three-CH2-longer molecule is larger and so boils higher, the gradual size effect on physical properties.

glossary.definition: A family of organic compounds sharing a functional group, whose successive members differ by CH2.
The atom or group of atoms that determines a molecule's physical and chemical properties.
The formula pattern shared by every member of a homologous series.
